text:
maria: seeing a sharp throughput drop in eu-west around 09:05 UTC, lots of worker restarts and a few GPU OOMs. CPU looks fine.
aj: noticed the same, tailing logs now. kernel selection retries spiking.
kevin: I have profiler drag output, looks like kernel flip between aten_cuda and our fused-kernel for decoder layers.
lia: are we getting small-batch surge from the routing layer? recent traffic shift from a customer caused many single-request batches.
sam: yes, routing metrics show 4x increase in single-token requests to model x-13k at 09:03. Batching heuristic didn't coalesce.
oncall-bot: Incident created: #1973600123 - throughput drop eu-west (assigned to oncall).
maria: logs show repeated KV cache evictions + large slab fragmentation on GPU: eviction churn in the allocator.
aj: paste of the allocator summary: ```
[GPU0] total_slabs 2048 used_slabs 1739 free_slabs 309 frag_ratio 0.72
[evict] rounds=127 evicted_pages=4123 reclaimed_bytes=1.2GB
[oom] worker_restart_count=14
```
kevin: profiler snapshot (sample): ```
hotspots:
  fused_attention_kernel 48.3% (latency spike)
  aten_cuda_attn 22.1% (fallback)
  kv_cache_touch 12.4%
  allocator_free 6.2%
```
lia: that frag_ratio is nasty. suspecting stranded allocations from failed coalesces during tiny batches + kernel swap leaving different memory layout.
sam: also saw a pattern: when kernel fallback happens, the KV touch pattern changes and forces page re-layout -> eviction loop.
maria: rollback? can we force deterministic kernel selection to fused-kernel for that model to stabilize?
kevin: we can patch routing rules to prefer fused-kernel for seq_len <= 128 and batch <= 8. quick patch looks safe.
aj: pushing canary to eu-west pool-3 with kernel pin and raised kv-cache TTL to reduce evictions.
deploy-bot: deploying canary to pool-3 (eu-west) with tags: kernel=fused-p3, kv_cache_ttl=60s.
sam: after canary deploy, throughput recovered ~35% in that pool within 3 minutes.
maria: good. but other pools still seeing restarts from the noisy tenant.
lia: recommend a short-term mitigation: throttle max single-request burst per-tenant and increase batching latency window by +10ms to give coalescer time.
aj: did that for the tenant via routing policy: max_concurrent_single=8, batch_wait_ms += 10.
kevin: also added a gated fallback: if allocator frag >0.65 then pin kernel to fused and disable aten fallback for 30s per host.
sam: FYI the noisy tenant is sending high-frequency embeddings interleaved with short generations; mixing workloads seems to increase small-batch churn.
maria: can we create a perf profile comparing before/after? kevin, can you attach pprof cpu+gpu snapshot?
kevin: attached short `nvprof` snapshot excerpt: ```
Time(%)  Calls  Avg(ms)  Name
48.3    13000  0.72     fused_attention_kernel
22.1     9000  0.35     aten_cuda_attn
...```
sam: we should also add a guard in the batcher: if detect >60% single-request ratio, switch to eager coalescing mode (longer window) for that route.
lia: agree. long term: need allocator defragmentation pass and better kernel memory reuse compat between fused and aten variants.
maria: action items: 1) keep canary pinned for 30m (aj) 2) tenant throttled + batch window increased (sam) 3) add single-request ratio guard (kevin) 4) follow-up RFC for allocator defrag + kernel memory contract (lia).
aj: canary running, metrics dashboard linked: https://grafana.internal/arena/d/xyz/oom-investigation (private link).
sre: marking incident acknowledged, paging logs to incident channel for postmortem.
deploy-bot: canary: success, 3/3 nodes healthy.
maria: after 45m, global throughput still ~8% below baseline but worker restarts stopped in canary nodes.
kevin: beginning work on single-request ratio guard PR, will add tests for ordering guarantees.
lia: I'll open the RFC and include proposed API for kernel memory compatibility.
sam: we should also run a synthetic noisy-tenant test in staging to reproduce fragmentation pattern. will schedule.
maria: thanks team. I'll start a short postmortem draft and include the profiler snippets and allocator stats.
aj: logging more detailed allocator traces for next 24h.
sre: closing timeline note: root cause = small-batch surge + kernel fallback causing memory layout mismatch -> allocator fragmentation -> evictions -> OOM -> worker restarts. mitigations taken and long-term work scheduled.
maria: +1. Will update once RFC is in.
kevin: PR link: https://git.internal/repo/pulls/842 (in progress)
lia: RFC link: https://docs.internal/rfcs/allocator-defrag-kernel-contract (draft)
maria: last note: alert configured to trigger when worker_restart_rate > 5/min AND frag_ratio > 0.6 so we can catch earlier.
sam: adding canary load test results to the incident doc.
oncall-bot: Incident 1973600123 status: mitigated -> monitoring (updated by maria).
